WHAT YOU’RE SEEING

A LITTLE EXPERIMENT

Make the clocks disagree.

Move a stationary observer closer to the black hole. Compare how much time passes locally and far away. Nothing special needs to happen to the observer’s own watch.

Inside this model +

The Schwarzschild radius is rₛ = 2GM/c² ≈ 2.953 km per solar mass. A stationary clock at radius r runs at √(1 − rₛ/r) times the rate of a clock very far away.

This compares stationary observers outside a spherical, non-rotating mass. It omits orbital motion, black hole spin, and frame dragging. The observer is held in place rather than freely falling. Hovering becomes increasingly difficult near the event horizon.

The neutron star has a chosen fixed radius; its interior and equation of state are not modeled. The rotating beams illustrate the pulsar lighthouse idea. Their display spin is slowed and is not used in the clock calculation.

Diagrams, beams, and any halo are illustrative, not telescope images or relativistic ray tracing. Background: NASA’s guide to stars ↗
